items.summary: The All India Students' Association (AISA) called its Mandi House demonstration (5:15 PM, Oct 16, led by president Neha Bora) around three explicit demands: the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, the revocation of the SIR electoral-roll revision, and the scrapping of the 2023 Election Commissioner Appointment Act. AISA activists and students later marched from Mandi House toward Connaught Place with the tricolour; Bora and others were detained at the Mandi House roundabout.
items.title: AISA's Mandi House demo pressed three demands: CEC resignation, SIR rollback, scrapping the 2023 EC Appointment Act

items.summary: AISA functionaries confirmed advocates were able to meet detained AISA president Neha Bora at the RK Puram police station. AISA says she has been suffering health issues in recent days and urgently needs medication that custodial officers are declining to provide; authorities gave no confirmation on her release. This is the first reported legal-team contact with Bora since her detention at Mandi House (~5:40 PM IST, Oct 16). No second outlet has carried this yet.
items.title: Advocates meet detained Neha Bora at RK Puram; AISA says medication being denied, no word on release

items.summary: Three on-topic BJP counter-side statements on Friday: (1) BJP leader and former MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh alleged in Unnao that Elon Musk is 'orchestrating' CJP's Tiranga march as 'a massive conspiracy against our nation' and claimed the march aimed to intimidate the Supreme Court — he provided no evidence (7Globe; News Pulse/Civaro Pulse; Trendkia live blog). (2) BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi called the Connaught Place rally a 'conspiracy to destabilise' India's economy during the festive season and urged students not to become 'pawns' (LatestLY, first appeared 10:28 PM IST Oct 16). (3) Delhi BJP president Harsh Malhotra praised Delhi Police's handling of the event and alleged 'foreign sponsors' behind CJP, adding that Dipke may be released or produced before a magistrate on Saturday (IANS via hi INDiA).
items.title: BJP counter-offensive Friday: Brij Bhushan alleges Musk is 'orchestrating' the protests; Trivedi alleges economy-destabilisation plot; Delhi BJP claims 'foreign sponsors'

items.summary: Bengaluru police first denied CJP permission for the 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march at Town Hall on Friday morning, citing Karnataka High Court directions confining protests to Freedom Park plus traffic concerns (inshorts/Times Now; articlesinfos; PTI via Trendkia). Later the same day, police granted conditional approval: the march — organised with Jagruta Karnataka, AISA Karnataka and My Vote, My Right in support of Das and Ranka — proceeded from Town Hall to the Quit India Memorial with hundreds braving persistent rain. Conditions imposed: no protest slogans against political parties/organisations/communities/individuals, and protest placards restricted at the destination (Mirror Now).
items.title: Bengaluru: Town Hall Tiranga march denied in the morning, then granted conditional approval — hundreds marched in rain
